papers.name: Paper 1 Living in the UK Today

topics.name: Theme 1.1 Landscapes of the UK
points: 1.1.1 Upland, lowland and glaciated landscapes of the UK: distribution and characteristics (geology, climate, human activity)
1.1.2 Geomorphic processes: weathering, mass movement, erosion, transport and deposition
1.1.3 River landforms and how they change from source: waterfall, gorge, V-shaped valley, floodplain, levee, meander, oxbow lake
1.1.4 Coastal landforms: headland, bay, cave, arch, stack, beach, spit
1.1.5 Case study of one UK river basin: processes, landforms, human activity and management
1.1.5 Case study of one UK coastal landscape: processes, landforms, human activity and management

topics.name: Theme 1.2 People of the UK
points: 1.2.1 UK trade: major trading partners, principal exports and imports
1.2.2 Diversity and inequality: employment, income, life expectancy, education, ethnicity and broadband access
1.2.3 Causes of uneven development in the UK; case study of growth and/or decline in one UK place or region
1.2.4 UK population change since 1900, Demographic Transition Model and ageing population
1.2.4 21st-century immigration flows and their social and economic impacts
1.2.5 Suburbanisation, counter-urbanisation and re-urbanisation: causes and consequences
1.2.6 Major UK city case study: city in its region, country and world; migration; ways of life
1.2.6 Major UK city case study: contemporary challenges (housing, transport, waste) and a sustainable strategy

topics.name: Theme 1.3 UK Environmental Challenges
points: 1.3.1 UK climate: air masses, North Atlantic Drift, continentality and extreme weather
1.3.2 Case study of one UK flood event caused by extreme weather: causes, effects and management
1.3.3 Human use and modification of UK ecosystems for food, energy and water
1.3.4 Renewable and non-renewable energy sources and their contribution to UK supply
1.3.5 Changing UK energy supply and demand since 1950; role of government and international organisations
1.3.5 Sustainable energy strategies at local and national scales; impacts of renewable energy development
1.3.5 Future UK energy supply: role of non-renewables and economic, political and environmental factors

topics.name: Theme 2.1 Ecosystems of the Planet
points: 2.1.1 Ecosystems: interdependent abiotic and biotic components
2.1.2 Global distribution and characteristics of polar regions, coral reefs, grasslands, temperate forests, tropical rainforests and hot deserts
2.1.3 Locations of the major tropical rainforests
2.1.4 Locations of the major warm water coral reefs
2.1.5 Nutrient and water cycles in tropical rainforests; nutrient cycling in coral reefs
2.1.5 Tropical rainforest case study: interdependence, value, threats and sustainable management
2.1.5 Coral reef case study: interdependence, value, threats and sustainable management

topics.name: Theme 2.2 People of the Planet
points: 2.2.1 Definitions of development and development indicators (GNI per capita, HDI, internet users); ACs, EDCs and LIDCs
2.2.2 Causes of uneven development: colonialism, trade, and the role of aid
2.2.3 LIDC/EDC case study: location, environment, resources, politics and relations with other states
2.2.3 LIDC/EDC case study: trade, international investment, population and employment structure
2.2.3 LIDC/EDC case study: education, healthcare, technology, one aid project and Rostow's model
2.2.4 Urbanisation: city, megacity and world city; distribution of megacities; urban growth rates
2.2.5 Rapid urbanisation in LIDCs: causes and consequences
2.2.6 Major LIDC/EDC city case study: influences, migration, ways of life, challenges and a sustainable strategy

topics.name: Theme 2.3 Environmental Threats to our Planet
points: 2.3.1 Climate change since the start of the Quaternary and since 1000 AD; evidence for climate change
2.3.2 Natural causes of climate change and the human-enhanced greenhouse effect
2.3.3 Current consequences of climate change across the planet
2.3.4 Global atmospheric circulation, climatic regions and extreme weather
2.3.5 Causes, distribution, frequency and change over time of tropical storms and drought
2.3.6 Case study of one El Niño/La Niña drought: development, effects and adaptation

topics.name: Section A 3.1 to 3.4 Geographical skills (and synoptic questions)
points: 3.1 Cartographic skills: constructing maps, cross-sections, coordinates, scale and distance
3.1 OS maps: gradient, contours and spot heights; GIS data
3.2 Graphical skills: selecting, constructing and interpreting graphs and charts
3.3 Numerical skills: number, area, scale, units, proportion, ratio, percentages
3.3 Statistical skills: central tendency, spread, quartiles, IQR; bivariate data, lines of best fit, interpolation and extrapolation
3.3 Designing data collection; identifying weaknesses and drawing conclusions from data
3.4 Visual and written sources: images, written articles and bias; evaluating sources
Synoptic questions drawing on Papers 1 and 2

topics.name: Section B Fieldwork
points: Questions suited to fieldwork and enquiry processes
Fieldwork techniques and methods, including observation and measurement
Processing and presenting fieldwork data as maps, graphs and diagrams
Analysing and explaining field data using case studies and theories
Drawing evidenced conclusions from fieldwork data
Critically reflecting on data, methods, conclusions and knowledge gained
